mechanic: A single static (non-scroll-driven) black hero: a 120% bottom-anchored looping background video, a blurred black pill scrim, and a centered z-stacked column of a two-line Inter/Instrument-Serif italic headline, Manrope subtitle, and two pill CTAs, capped by a glassmorphic backdrop-blur frame holding the product dashboard image.
techDelivery: React component spec authored with inline/utility styling and exact pixel geometry (fonts Inter, Instrument Serif, Manrope, Cabin assumed loaded via the host; no animation library or scroll engine declared — the hero is statically composed).
reskinNotes: Five distinct typefaces are mixed for effect and all four are load-bearing: Inter (headline line 1, medium 76px), Instrument Serif (headline line 2, italic 76px — the serif/sans contrast is the signature, so the accent face must be a true italic display serif), Manrope (nav links + subtitle + the nav Sign In/Get Started buttons), and Cabin (only the two hero CTA labels) — Cabin has no colorRole or token and is referenced solely by the CTA buttons, so it is easy to miss. Headline layout is font-metric dependent: 76px at letter-spacing -2px and line-height 1.15 across two lines at max-width 871px, so a wider display/serif face or longer translated copy will rewrap or overflow. The two purples (#7b39fc primary accent, #2b2344 dark-purple secondary CTA) plus the near-duplicate off-whites (#fafafa nav button text vs #f6f7f9 subtitle/secondary-CTA text at 90% opacity) and the #d4d4d4 1px Sign In border are scattered as literal hex values rather than tokens, so retinting means find-replacing each literal. All copy is hardcoded: 'LOGOIPSUM', nav items ['Home','Services','Reviews','Contact us'], 'Sign In'/'Get Started', the headline 'Automate repetitive.' / 'Focus on growth.', the AI-agent subtitle, and 'Get Started Free' / 'Watch 2min Demo'. Geometry is fixed in pixels (120% video scale, 801x384 + 77.5px-blur pill at top:215px, 1440px navbar, 1163px dashboard frame), so the layout is tuned for desktop and the blurred-pill scrim assumes the headline sits over it.
